reason: The dispersion book is working: NAV +3.60% vs SPY +2.50%, max drawdown -6.5%, and the 34.5% SPY short keeps net index beta near zero, so the P&L is coming from idiosyncratic legs, which is the mandate. Research (WebSearch) supports the core legs. CME, the largest leg (+10.3%), reported a record Q3 on 10-21: revenue $1.74B (+13% y/y), adj. EPS $3.02 vs ~$2.98 consensus, ADV +16% to 29.4M, market data +20%; the shares dipped premarket on expense guidance, but the rates/volatility volume thesis was confirmed by hard data. NEM (-7.1%) reported a record Q3 for adjusted net income on 10-22 (~1.3M oz, $1.9B FCF, guidance and improved cost outlook reaffirmed), so the gold-FCF thesis is intact and the drawdown looks like gold-price beta rather than a company problem; I could not confirm this week's gold move, and the -20% stop is still ~13% away. AKAM (-8.0%) is the weakest thesis: HSBC cut it to Hold (PT $171->$123) on cloud-infrastructure margins and capex, and it fell ~8% on 10-14. But it is only 5% weight, the -18% stop is ~10% below the mark, and Q3 earnings (est. ~11-05) are exactly the kind of idiosyncratic event this book is built to hold. Cutting it ahead of the print would turn a dispersion book into a momentum book. CI reports 10-29 pre-market and MCK ~11-04; those single-name earnings events are the dispersion this book exists to harvest, and each is a 6-6.5% leg with stops in place. No stop or take-profit is near triggering. Replacing or resizing would pay frictions and reset entry fills for no thesis change, so holding beats trading. Limits: I found no coverage of the HII earnings date or of gold/NEM price action for the week of 10-19; SLB, DG and TRV were judged on the packet marks alone.
